what_it_does: Self-driving cars and robots perceive the world as clouds of 3D points from lidar sensors, and a key step is finding each point's nearest neighbors — a search done by walking a binary tree structure called a k-d tree. Modern processors handle repetitive math quickly by working on many values simultaneously (SIMD — Single Instruction, Multiple Data), but k-d tree traversal for different query points diverges at deeper tree levels, so many of those parallel slots sit idle. Caravan batches similar queries together so they share early tree steps in parallel, then adds two new processor instructions that let the hardware quickly compact and rearrange the still-active query slots at the point of divergence, keeping the parallel pipeline full throughout.
